requirements.rationale: A backup that misses controller settings, keys or field parameters may not get the system running again. The owner needs to know what a complete backup holds and how to keep it safe.
requirements.evidencePrompt: Deliverable: backup procedures for the automation solution. Check the backup method, the data covered (from operating system files and keys through applications, databases and logs to network, controller and field instrument settings), offsite storage advice and the rule on changes during a backup.

requirements.title: Restore instructions
requirements.hint: The provider can give the owner written instructions for bringing the automation solution, or single components, back to normal operation from backup, including what to do if things have changed since.
requirements.rationale: Restores are often done under pressure after a failure or incident. Clear instructions, covering awkward cases too, cut downtime and warn where a restore may be incomplete.
requirements.evidencePrompt: Deliverable: restore instructions for the full system and for components. Check they deal with abnormal cases, such as an architecture changed since the backup, and apply to simulators as well as live systems.

requirements.title: Handling of portable backup media
requirements.hint: The provider can give the owner documentation on how portable backup media is controlled, stored and protected, in line with the owner's own policies and procedures.
requirements.rationale: Backup media holds a full copy of the system, often with credentials and configuration. Lost or tampered media can block recovery or hand an attacker what they need.
requirements.evidencePrompt: Deliverable: backup media handling procedure. Ask how media is labelled, stored, moved, accessed and destroyed, and how this fits the owner's policies.

requirements.title: Checking a backup succeeded
requirements.hint: The provider can give the owner documentation explaining how to confirm that a system backup has completed successfully and can be relied on.
requirements.rationale: A backup job can report success yet leave a copy that will not restore. A defined check gives the owner confidence before the copy is ever needed.
requirements.evidencePrompt: Deliverable: backup verification instructions. Ask for records of recent checks and what they test, such as completion logs, checksums or trial restores.

requirements.title: Full backup and restore demonstrated
requirements.hint: The provider can demonstrate a complete backup of the automation solution and a restore from it to a working system, or a partial run if the owner prefers, with database rollback handled properly.
requirements.rationale: Only a successful restore proves the backup arrangement works. Showing it before an emergency exposes gaps while there is still time to fix them.
requirements.evidencePrompt: Ask for records of a backup and restore demonstration or test, its scope (full or partial) and result, and steps taken for databases, such as suspending automatic rollback during the backup.

requirements.title: Backups follow the owner's schedule
requirements.hint: The provider can carry out backups of the automation solution on the owner's schedule and in line with the owner's restore and disaster recovery objectives.
requirements.rationale: How often to back up depends on how much data and configuration the owner can afford to lose. Working to the owner's schedule ties the provider's work to that business decision.
requirements.evidencePrompt: Ask for the owner's backup schedule and recovery objectives, and backup logs showing the provider has kept to them.

requirements.title: Operation continues during backup
requirements.hint: The provider can demonstrate that taking a backup does not disturb the normal running of the automation solution, including control of the process.
requirements.rationale: If backups slow or interrupt control, staff will avoid running them. Showing they are safe to take while the system is live keeps backups happening on time.
requirements.evidencePrompt: Ask for test or commissioning records showing backups taken during operation, with performance or alarm data showing no effect on control.

requirements.title: Audit logging of backup and restore
requirements.hint: The provider can give the owner documentation on how to set up and keep audit logs that record every backup and restore activity on the automation solution.
requirements.rationale: Logs of when backups and restores ran, who ran them and with what result give the owner evidence of good practice and a trail to follow if something goes wrong.
requirements.evidencePrompt: Deliverable: documentation on configuring and maintaining backup and restore audit logs. Ask to see sample log entries showing time, person and outcome.

requirements.title: Disaster recovery plan
requirements.hint: The provider can document a recommended disaster recovery plan: likely scenarios and their effect, how to recover and reintegrate failed components, and the minimum setup needed to rebuild the whole system.
requirements.rationale: After a major cyber incident or site loss, the owner needs a worked-out route back to operation that does not depend on equipment that may itself have been lost.
requirements.evidencePrompt: Deliverable: disaster recovery plan for the automation solution. Check it covers scenarios including cyber attack, recovery steps, the minimum architecture for a full rebuild, and where restore tools such as a test bench or offline engineering tools are kept.

achievedScale._note: ONE control per requirement. Consultant picks one value. 'not-met' is the bottom of the scale; ML1-4 are increasing maturity; 'unknown' and 'na' are non-scoring states shown alongside.

targetOverlay._note: Optional. Off by default. When enabled, each requirement gains an optional target ML, usually set from the contract. When off, the report shows the achieved-ML profile only.

_contentNote: 123 requirements (72 base requirements, 51 enhancements) across 12 functional areas, ids from the standard. Content is paraphrased from the licensed standard in our own words; verbatimText is empty by design. 'kind' (BR/RE), 'parentId' (an enhancement's base requirement) and 'deliverableDoc' (a document is delivered to the asset owner) are carried for the views; the scorer ignores them. Themes reuse the eight 62443-2-1:2024 themes.
_scopingNote: elementScoping: a whole functional area can be set out of scope per target (target.elementScope). Its rows then score as N/A, and their answers are kept.
seriesContext: ISA/IEC 62443 is a series of standards divided by who is responsible for what. This part, 62443-2-4, covers the service provider who integrates or maintains an automation solution for an asset owner. It is the companion of 62443-2-1, which covers the asset owner's own security program, and of 62443-4-1, which covers the product supplier's development process.
